'''Walter Kutschera''' (born 1939) is an Austrian [[physicist]].

==Biography==
Kutschera was born in [[Vienna]], [[Austria]] in 1939. In 1965 he got his Ph.D. in [[experimental physics]] from the Austrian [[University of Graz]]. Starting from next year and for the whole 27 after, he was working in different institutions researching [[nuclear physics]], majority of which had to do with tandem accelerators. In 1978 he taught Experimental physics at [[University of Tokyo]] in [[Tokyo]], Japan for one year, followed by 14 years of work at [[Argonne National Laboratory]] in [[Chicago]]. In 1980 he focused his research on the study of ''isotope language''. He became Senior Scientist in 1986, in the end of his teachings in Illinois. Later, he worked at [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in Rehovot, and accepted an invitation to [[Jerusalem]], [[Israel]] for one year, where he taught at [[Racah Institute of Physics]], a division of the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem|Hebrew University]]. From 1993 to 2007 he worked as Professor of Physics at the [[University of Vienna]] and was a head of [[Isotope Research and Nuclear Physics]].<ref name="univie">{{Cite web|last=Figl|first=Andreas|title=Walter Kutschera Homepage|url=http://homepage.univie.ac.at/walter.kutschera/|access-date=2021-05-18|website=homepage.univie.ac.at|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220629165235/https://homepage.univie.ac.at/walter.kutschera/|archive-date=2022-06-29}}</ref>

He founded [[Vienna Environmental Research Accelerator]], a universal facility which operates since 1996 and is a part of [[Accelerator mass spectrometry]]. The construction was based on 3-MV model of [[pelletron]] tandem accelerator, which was one of his key interests. In 1999 he became the president of the [[Austrian Physical Society]], but had it only for one year. Four years later he became the Dean of [[Faculty of Physics]] in University of Vienna, and 2 years later became its Vice-Dean. The same year he was awarded with a [[Decoration of Honour for Services to the Republic of Austria]]. In 2008 he was promoted to [[Professor|Emeritus Professor]] of Physics.<ref name=univie/> In 2010 he was awarded by [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]] with an [[Erwin Schrödinger Prize]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://derstandard.at/1285200586246/Ausgezeichnet-Physiker-Walter-Kutschera-erhaelt-Erwin-Schroedinger-Preis-2010|title=Physiker Walter Kutschera erhält Erwin-Schrödinger-Preis 2010|trans-title=Physicist Walter Kutschera receives Erwin Schrödinger Prize 2010|work=[[Der Standard]]|date=October 11, 2010|accessdate=December 6, 2014|language=de}}</ref> and a year later he became a [[Fellow of the American Association]] award for the [[Advancement of Science]]. Besides physics, his other researched include works in [[archaeology]], [[art]], [[atmospheric sciences|atmospheric science]], [[atomic physics|atomic]] and [[molecular physics]], [[biomedicine]], [[environmental science|environmental physics]], [[medical jurisprudence|forensic medicine]], [[Egyptology]], [[geochronology]], [[geomorphology]], [[geophysics]], [[glaciology]], [[groundwater dating]], [[nuclear astrophysics]], [[nuclear physics]], [[oceanography]], and  [[paleoclimatology]].<ref name=univie/>

==Works==
Starting from 2004 he has written three works and was a co-author of many others:<ref name=univie/> 
Author:
*[[2004 in literature|2004]] — ''Tracing Noble Gas Radionuclides in the Environment''
*[[2008 in literature|2008]] — ''A homage to ECAART-9 and Florence''
*[[2010 in literature|2010]] — ''AMS and Climate Change''

Co-author:
*[[2004 in literature|2004]] — ''VERA, an AMS Facility for "all" Isotopes''
*2004 — ''Direct Dating of Early Upper Palaeolithic Human Remains from Mladec''
*[[2005 in literature|2005]] — ''Progress in isotope analysis at ultra-trace level by AMS''
*2005 — ''AMS Radiocarbon Dating of Bone Samples from the Xinzhai Site in China''
*2005 — ''Experimental and Theoretical Evidence for Long-Lived Molecular Hydrogen Anions H2 and D2''
*[[2006 in literature|2006]] — ''Radiocarbon Determination of Particulate Organic Carbon in Non-Temperated, Alpine Glacier Ice''
*2006 — ''Chronology for the Aegean Late Bronze Age''
*[[2007 in literature|2007]] — ''Exotic Negative Molecules in AMS''
*2007 — ''Radiocarbon Dating of the Peruvian Chachapoya/Inca Site at the Laguna de los Condores''
*[[2008 in literature|2008]] — ''PIXE measurements of renaissance silverpoint drawings at VERA''
*[[2009 in literature|2009]] — ''Dating the Santorini/Thera Eruption by Radiocarbon: Further Discussion (AD 2006-2007)''
*[[2010 in literature|2010]] — ''Search for a Superheavy Nuclide with A=292 and Neutron-Deficient Thorium Isotopes in Natural Thorianite''
*[[2011 in literature|2011]] — ''Upper Limits for the Existence of Long-Lived Isotopes of Roentgenium in Natural Gold''
*2011 — ''Ultrasensitive Search for Long-Lived Superheavy Nuclides in the Mass Range A = 288 to A = 300 in Natural Pt, Pb, and Bi''
*[[2012 in literature|2012]] — ''The Age of Olfactory Bulb Neurons in Humans''
